selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at this UNESCO-listed square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform as the sun sets. Sample street food like harira soup, msemen flatbread, and fresh-squeezed orange juice from the surrounding stalls.

experiences.name: Camel Trek and Sahara Desert Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga, watching the sunset paint the sand in vivid oranges and reds. Spend the night in a traditional Berber desert camp under a breathtaking canopy of stars, enjoy a tagine dinner around a campfire, and wake up for a spectacular sunrise over the dunes.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Guided Tour of the Medina and Souks
experiences.description: Navigate the labyrinthine medieval alleyways of Marrakech's ancient Medina with a knowledgeable local guide. Discover hidden riads, bustling artisan workshops, and vibrant souks selling spices, leather goods, ceramics, and handwoven textiles. Visit the iconic Bahia Palace and Ben Youssef Madrasa along the way.

experiences.name: Moroccan Cooking Class in a Traditional Riad
experiences.description: Learn the art of Moroccan cuisine in an authentic riad kitchen. A local chef guides you through selecting fresh ingredients at the market, then teaches you to prepare classic dishes like chicken bastilla, lamb tagine with preserved lemons, and traditional mint tea. Enjoy the meal you've created in a beautifully tiled courtyard.

experiences.name: Hike in the Atlas Mountains and Berber Village Visit
experiences.description: Embark on a guided day hike through the dramatic High Atlas Mountains, passing terraced fields, walnut groves, and cascading waterfalls. Visit the traditional Berber village of Imlil, meet local families, and enjoy a home-cooked lunch of freshly baked bread and amlou (almond-argan dip) while learning about centuries-old mountain culture.
experiences.location: Imlil Valley, High Atlas Mountains, near Marrakech

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange a petit taxi or pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Settle into your room, freshen up, and get a good night's rest ahead of a full day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.dinner: Grab a quick snack from a 24-hour convenience store or hotel reception if available — budget ~30 MAD (~$3)

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate taxi fare before getting in — a standard petit taxi from Marrakech airport to the medina area costs roughly 70–100 MAD. Avoid touts and use licensed taxis only. Exchange a small amount of currency (MAD) at the airport for immediate needs.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Marrakech adventure with a hearty budget breakfast near the hotel, then walk or take a short taxi to Djemaa el-Fna square. Explore the iconic square in the morning when it is calm and photogenic. Visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque (exterior viewing, free) and stroll through the surrounding gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive deep into the Marrakech Medina — wander the souks (Souk Semmarine, Souk des Épices) and practice your bargaining skills. Visit the free exterior of Ben Youssef Madrasa area and explore the dyers' quarter (Souk Sabbaghin). Stop at Maison de la Photographie (entry ~50 MAD) for rooftop views and cultural insight.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a vibrant night market. Watch street performers, snake charmers, and storytellers. Eat dinner from the open-air food stalls right on the square — one of the most authentic budget experiences in Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Café de France or a local café near the medina — mint tea, msemen (Moroccan pancake), and amlou (almond-argan dip) for ~25–35 MAD
meals.lunch: Street food in the souks — harira soup, a sandwich with kefta, or a fresh-squeezed orange juice for ~30–50 MAD total
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — grilled meats, couscous, or tagine for ~60–80 MAD. Stall No. 1 is famous but any numbered stall offers similar quality at budget prices.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the medina involves a lot of cobblestone walking. Keep your bag close in crowded souk areas. Bargain confidently; initial prices are often 3–4x the fair value.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD) — a stunning 19th-century palace with ornate Moroccan architecture, carved cedar ceilings, and lush courtyards. Arrive early to avoid crowds. Afterward, head to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) to explore its historic streets and the Lazama Synagogue (free or small donation).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a beautifully preserved royal necropolis dating to the 16th century. Then visit the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) for sweeping views and fascinating history. End the afternoon at the Mellah market for local spices, dried fruits, and nuts at wholesale prices.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through the Kasbah neighborhood. Enjoy a budget dinner at a local restaurant off the tourist trail, then return to the hotel to pack for the Sahara journey beginning tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a local bakery near the hotel — khobz bread, olive oil, and coffee for ~20–30 MAD
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Clock Marrakech (a local institution) — camel burger or veggie option for ~60–80 MAD
meals.dinner: Restaurant Haj Boujemaa near the Mellah — traditional Moroccan tagine or couscous for ~50–70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The combo of Bahia Palace, Saadian Tombs, and El Badi Palace is walkable within the southern medina. A guided walking tour of this area can be arranged cheaply through your hotel (~100–150 MAD for a local guide). Book your Sahara desert tour tonight if not already arranged.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure (around 07:00) from Marrakech on a shared budget group tour to the Sahara Desert via Ait Benhaddou and the Draa Valley. This classic route crosses the High Atlas Mountains through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation). Stop at a roadside café in the mountains for a quick tea break with panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ait Benhaddou (UNESCO World Heritage Site) around midday — explore this ancient ksar (fortified village) that has served as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Entry is free to wander the exterior; a small fee (~10 MAD) to cross the river and enter the ksar. Continue driving through the Draa Valley's stunning palm groves and kasbahs toward Ouarzazate.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Ouarzazate by late afternoon. Check into a budget guesthouse (riad-style, ~150–200 MAD per night). Explore the town briefly, visit the Atlas Studios exterior (the world's largest film studio), and enjoy a quiet dinner at a local restaurant before an early night ahead of the desert push tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — bread, jam, and coffee (~20 MAD) or pack snacks from a medina bakery
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Ait Benhaddou village — tagine with bread for ~50–70 MAD
meals.dinner: Restaurant near your Ouarzazate guesthouse — harira soup, tagine, and mint tea for ~60–80 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Shared group tours from Marrakech to Sahara (3-day/2-night) typically cost 600–900 MAD per person and include transport, basic accommodation, and camel ride. Book through a reputable agency in the medina or via your hotel. This is significantly cheaper than private tours. Bring a light jacket — the Atlas Mountains can be cold in March.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning drive from Ouarzazate continuing southeast through the stunning Dadès Gorge and Todra Gorge area. Stop at the Todra Gorge (entry free) — 300-meter-high canyon walls that are breathtaking and perfect for a short hike along the riverbed. Local vendors sell fresh-squeezed juice and snacks at the gorge entrance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the journey toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes — Morocco's most spectacular Saharan landscape. Arrive in Merzouga village in the mid-afternoon. Check bags into a budget desert camp or guesthouse at the dune base. Meet your camel guide and begin your camel trek into the Sahara (included in most group tour packages).
day_by_day.evening: Ride camels into the heart of the Erg Chebbi dunes to reach your desert camp by sunset. Watch the sunset over the Sahara — one of the most awe-inspiring experiences in the world. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner at camp around a campfire, with live Gnawa drumming and music under an extraordinary star-filled sky. Sleep in a desert camp tent.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Ouarzazate — bread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea (~25–35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or a quick stop at a roadside café near Tinghir (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Included in desert camp package — traditional Berber couscous or tagine with vegetables, mint tea, and fresh fruit (~included or ~80–100 MAD if paying separately)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headscarf or shemagh to protect against sand. Temperatures in March can drop significantly at night in the desert (near 5–10°C) — bring a warm layer. Charge all devices before leaving Merzouga as camps have limited or no electricity. The camel ride is typically 1–1.5 hours each way.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (around 05:30) to climb a dune and watch the Sahara sunrise — an unforgettable golden spectacle over an endless sea of sand. Take time to sandboard down the dunes (boards available at camp for ~30–50 MAD) or simply explore on foot. Camel trek back to Merzouga village after breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Merzouga village and visit a local Gnawa musician's home for an informal cultural exchange (often arranged by camp hosts, free or small tip). Begin the long return journey toward Marrakech — passing through Rissani (birthplace of the Alaouite dynasty), the Ziz Valley, and Erfoud (known for fossil markets). Stop to browse fossils and ammonite crafts at Erfoud market.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight stop in Midelt or Errachidia — check into a budget hotel (~100–150 MAD). Enjoy a quiet dinner at a local restaurant and rest for the final drive back to Marrakech tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp — Berber bread (khobz), olive oil, argan oil, honey, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Roadside café stop in Rissani or Erfoud — harira, kefta sandwich, or tagine for ~40–60 MAD
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Midelt — lamb tagine or beef kefta with bread and tea for ~55–75 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The return journey from Merzouga to Marrakech is approximately 8–10 hours with stops. Most group tours include this return journey. Erfoud's fossil market is worth a brief stop — ammonite coasters and trilobite specimens make affordable souvenirs (bargain hard, start at 30–40% of asking price).

day_by_day.morning: Morning drive back through the High Atlas Mountains toward Marrakech, arriving mid-morning. Drop bags at the hotel and head straight to the Majorelle Garden (entry ~70 MAD) — a stunning botanical garden and art deco villa once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. The vibrant cobalt-blue structures and exotic plants make it one of Marrakech's most photogenic spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon souvenir shopping in the medina souks. Pick up argan oil, spices, leather goods, or Berber jewelry as gifts. Visit the Mellah spice market for the best prices on cumin, ras el hanout, and saffron. Enjoy a final mint tea ceremony at a rooftop café overlooking the medina rooftops.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Marrakech — treat yourself to a slightly nicer budget restaurant for your last night. Return to the hotel, pack, and prepare for departure. If your flight departs late or the next day, enjoy one final walk around Djemaa el-Fna to soak in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel or hotel breakfast — coffee, msemen, and fresh orange juice for ~30–40 MAD
meals.lunch: Lunch at a rooftop café near Majorelle Garden — salad, sandwich, and fresh juice for ~60–80 MAD
meals.dinner: Restaurant Nomad in the medina (trendy but affordable) or Café des Épices — modern Moroccan cuisine for ~100–130 MAD per person as a farewell splurge

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden can get crowded after 10:00 — arrive right at opening (09:00) for the best experience. The YSL Museum adjacent to the garden costs ~100 MAD extra but is worth it for design and fashion enthusiasts. Keep ~200–300 MAD in cash for last-minute shopping and taxi to the airport. Confirm your airport taxi the night before.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take a pre-arranged airport transfer or a petit taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room. Light exploration of the hotel facilities if energy allows.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack at the hotel bar or restaurant if still open, or enjoy room service — try a simple Moroccan harira soup or a sandwich to wind down.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 simple. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid hassle at night. Exchange some currency to Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) at the airport kiosk. Marrakech medina taxis can negotiate aggressively at night — agree on a price before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. At around 10:00, head into the Marrakech Medina. Visit the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere — orange juice vendors, storytellers, and snake charmers set the scene. Stroll through the nearby souks (spice market, leather goods, lanterns).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with ornate courtyards and painted ceilings. Afterward, walk to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) to explore its distinctive architecture and the Lazama Synagogue. Stop at a local café for mint tea and pastilla.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna at dusk when the square transforms into a massive open-air food market with acrobats, musicians, and storytellers. Dine at one of the rooftop terraces overlooking the square for a dramatic view.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy Moroccan staples like msemen (flatbread), honey, argan oil, and fresh-squeezed orange juice.
meals.lunch: Café Clock Marrakech or a local souk café — try a tagine with chicken and preserved lemon (~60–80 MAD).
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant at Café des Épices or Le Grand Balcon du Café Glacier overlooking Djemaa el-Fna — grilled kefta, couscous, and Moroccan salads (~120–180 MAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the medina's narrow alleys can be uneven. Bargaining in souks is expected; start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep a small bag close to you in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit (9:00 AM) to the Saadian Tombs, a hidden 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917 (entry ~70 MAD). Then walk to the El Badi Palace ruins, a once-magnificent palace now hauntingly beautiful in its decay — look for the storks nesting on the ramparts (entry ~70 MAD). Great for history and photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Yves Saint Laurent Museum and the adjacent Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD combined), a vibrant cobalt-blue botanical oasis that inspired the famous fashion designer. Spend time among the cacti, pools, and exotic plants. Browse the small Berber Museum inside the garden.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxing hammam experience at a mid-range local hammam such as Hammam El Bacha or a riad hammam (~150–250 MAD for full scrub and steam). Afterward, enjoy a quiet dinner in the Gueliz (modern) district for a change of pace.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Majorelle Garden — pick up fresh bread, olives, cheese, and fruit from a nearby market stall (~40–60 MAD).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Al Fassia in Gueliz — an authentic Moroccan restaurant run entirely by women, known for excellent pastilla and slow-cooked tagines (~150–200 MAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Saadian Tombs early to beat the crowds. The Majorelle Garden can get busy by midday — aim to arrive right when it opens at 8:00 AM or after 3:00 PM. Book the hammam in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:00–7:00 AM) by private driver or shared minibus toward the Sahara Desert via the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) through the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at Ait Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the ancient earthen citadel on foot (entry free, guide optional ~100 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through the Draa Valley, passing rose-pink kasbahs, palm groves, and dramatic desert landscapes. Arrive in Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') by early afternoon. Brief stop at Taourirt Kasbah (entry ~20 MAD). Continue onward toward Merzouga/Erg Chebbi — arrive at your desert camp by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels at sunset for a 45–60 minute ride into the Erg Chebbi sand dunes — the golden light at dusk is spectacular. Arrive at your desert camp, enjoy Berber tea and music around the campfire under a sky full of stars.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or grab msemen and coffee from a roadside café before departure.
meals.lunch: Traditional restaurant in Ait Benhaddou or Ouarzazate — lamb tagine with prunes and almonds (~80–100 MAD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the desert camp — traditional Berber feast including harira soup, tagine, and couscous with drumming and live music under the stars (typically included in camp package).

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Marrakech to Merzouga is approximately 8–9 hours with stops. A private driver costs ~600–900 MAD and is more flexible than a shared bus. Book your desert camp in advance — mid-range camps with private tents and en-suite facilities run ~400–700 MAD per person per night.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (5:30 AM) to climb the dunes and watch the Sahara sunrise — one of the most breathtaking experiences in Morocco. The silence, the shifting colors from deep purple to fiery orange, and the endless sea of sand are unforgettable. Return to camp for breakfast. Optional: sandboarding down the dunes (~50–100 MAD equipment rental).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the small village of Merzouga to interact with local Berber families and learn about desert life. Explore the area around the dunes by quad bike or 4x4 for an adventurous perspective of the landscape (~200–350 MAD for 1-hour quad rental). Visit a local fossil shop — the region is rich in ancient marine fossils embedded in stone.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey toward the Atlas Mountains, stopping in Tinghir to visit the stunning Todra Gorge — dramatic 300m-high rock walls carved by the Todra River. Short walk through the gorge as the last light hits the canyon walls. Overnight in a mid-range guesthouse in Tinghir.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast — Moroccan flatbread, honey, jam, eggs, and mint tea.
meals.lunch: Local café in Merzouga village — camel burger or tagine (~70–90 MAD).
meals.dinner: Guesthouse dinner in Tinghir or local restaurant — harira, lamb chops with cumin, and fresh salads (~100–130 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headlamp for the pre-dawn dune climb. The sand can be cold at night and early morning — pack a light layer. Stay hydrated throughout the day as the desert air is very dry. Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the late afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: Morning hike deeper into Todra Gorge (the gorge narrows to just 10m wide in places) before the tour groups arrive. The towering red-orange walls and the sound of the river are extraordinary. Optional: beginner rock climbing with a local guide (~200–300 MAD). Drive through the scenic Dades Valley, known as the 'Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs', stopping at the dramatic Dades Gorge with its winding switchback roads.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Valley of Roses near El Kelaa M'Gouna — in mid-March, the roses may just be beginning to bloom (peak bloom is April). Visit a local rose cooperative to learn how rose water and rose oil are extracted. Continue driving back toward Marrakech via the Skoura Oasis, a vast palm grove dotted with ancient kasbahs. Stop at Amridil Kasbah for a quick visit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening. Check back into your hotel, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll through the medina. Enjoy a final evening in the city's electric atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Tinghir — eggs, flatbread, local honey.
meals.lunch: Roadside café in the Dades Valley — freshly made Berber omelette sandwich and mint tea (~40–60 MAD).
meals.dinner: Traditional Marrakech riad restaurant — splurge slightly on a set menu with pastilla, lamb tagine, and Moroccan desserts with live Gnawa music (~200–250 MAD per person). Try Riad Yima or Dar Moha.

day_by_day.notes: The Dades Gorge road has sharp switchbacks — if you're prone to motion sickness, take medication in advance. The Valley of Roses is more spectacular in April, but the cooperative and rose products are available year-round. Keep some cash for cooperative purchases — rose water and oils make excellent souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Last morning in Marrakech. Revisit any souks or sights you missed earlier in the week. Head to the Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of the largest Islamic colleges in North Africa — its intricate tilework, carved plaster, and cedar woodwork are breathtaking (entry ~70 MAD). Nearby, visit the small but fascinating Museum of Marrakech housed in a 19th-century palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping in the souks — leather goods, argan oil products, Berber rugs, lanterns, and spices. Bargain confidently and enjoy the experience. Enjoy a final mint tea ceremony at a rooftop café. Head back to the hotel to collect luggage and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on your departure time, enjoy a farewell dinner in Marrakech or head to the airport. Marrakech Menara Airport is approximately 15–20 minutes from the medina.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — savor your last Moroccan morning spread.
meals.lunch: Souk lunch at a local hole-in-the-wall spot — mechoui (slow-roasted lamb sold by weight) near the Rahba Kedima square (~60–80 MAD) — a true local experience.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Gueliz such as Comptoir Darna for a mix of Moroccan and international cuisine with live entertainment (~180–220 MAD per person), or a lighter option at a café near the airport if departing early.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Duty-free shops at Marrakech airport are limited — buy your argan oil and spices in the souks. Keep some MAD for a final taxi fare to the airport. Tipping is customary in Morocco — 10–15 MAD for café service, 20–50 MAD for guides.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Travel day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Travel day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. A private luxury transfer in a chauffeured Mercedes S-Class awaits. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and enjoy a welcome amenity: chilled Moroccan mint tea, rose water towels, and a curated fruit platter prepared by the concierge. Brief orientation with your dedicated butler to plan the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight
meals.dinner: Late-night private in-room dining: Harira soup, Bastilla bites, and a selection of Moroccan pastries arranged by the resort kitchen upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — rest is essential. Confirm all excursion bookings with your butler tonight. Ensure passports and travel documents are stored safely. Resort check-in is express and pre-arranged.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely start, enjoy a private guided tour of the UNESCO-listed Medina of Marrakech. Explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square, the ornate Koutoubia Mosque gardens, and the labyrinthine souks of spices, leather, and lanterns with your expert local guide. Visit the stunning Saadian Tombs — a hidden 16th-century royal necropolis.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private access visit to Bahia Palace, one of Morocco's finest 19th-century palaces, followed by an exclusive guided tour of the El Badi Palace ruins with panoramic rooftop views over the Medina. Stop at the Mellah (historic Jewish quarter) for a curated cultural walk.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset rooftop cocktails at a premier riad terrace in the Medina overlooking the Koutoubia minaret. Followed by an immersive private dinner experience at La Maison Arabe — Marrakech's legendary restaurant — featuring a traditional Moroccan tasting menu with live Gnawa music performance.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Moroccan breakfast at the resort: msemen flatbreads, amlou (argan & almond dip), fresh-squeezed orange juice, Medjool dates, and Berber omelettes.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Marrakech — a stylish rooftop restaurant in the Medina with contemporary Moroccan cuisine and panoramic views.
meals.dinner: Private tasting menu at La Maison Arabe — seven-course Moroccan feast including pastilla au pigeon, slow-cooked lamb tagine with preserved lemon, and orange blossom crème brûlée.

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for Medina visits (shoulders and knees covered). Wear comfortable walking shoes. Your guide will handle all entry fees and queue-jumping privileges. Carry a small amount of dirhams for souk browsing.

day_by_day.morning: Private early-access visit to the world-famous Majorelle Garden — a cobalt-blue botanical masterpiece once owned by Yves Saint Laurent — before the crowds arrive. Explore the adjacent Berber Museum and YSL Museum for a deep dive into art, fashion, and Moroccan heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a 3-hour royal hammam and spa journey at the resort or at the prestigious Heritage Spa — including a traditional black soap scrub (kessa), rhassoul clay mask, argan oil massage, and rose petal bath. Afternoon at leisure to explore the Gueliz (New City) neighborhood, visiting contemporary art galleries and designer boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset horse-drawn carriage (caleche) ride around the Medina walls followed by a rooftop dinner at Nomad or Dar Yacout — a legendary palace restaurant with candlelit courtyards, belly dancing, and a full Moroccan feast.

meals.breakfast: In-resort breakfast with a live cooking station: made-to-order Moroccan crepes, fresh pastries, Argan honey, and freshly brewed Moroccan coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café de France on Djemaa el-Fna square — Moroccan salads, briouats, and fresh-pressed juices while watching the square come alive.
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout — a legendary Marrakech institution set in a lavish riad with a 5-course Moroccan feast, rooftop views, and live Andalusian music.

day_by_day.notes: Book Majorelle Garden early-access through your butler in advance — slots are limited. The hammam session is best enjoyed mid-afternoon for maximum relaxation. Gueliz boutiques are ideal for premium Moroccan crafts and argan products.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for a scenic drive through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m). Stop at Berber villages en route for authentic local interactions and panoramic mountain photography. Visit the ancient Kasbah Telouet — a crumbling but magnificent 19th-century pasha's palace hidden in the mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Aït Benhaddou — the most spectacular fortified ksar (village) in Morocco, featured in Game of Thrones and Gladiator. Enjoy a private guided tour of the ancient earthen citadel with your expert historian guide. Optional short hike to the hilltop granary for sweeping valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech by private transfer as the sun sets over the Atlas. Relaxed evening at the resort — enjoy the pool terrace, a nightcap at the resort bar, and an early night to prepare for the Sahara journey tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast box prepared by the resort: croissants, Moroccan cheese, fresh fruit, and thermos of mint tea for the mountain journey.
meals.lunch: Traditional Berber lunch at a family-run riad near Aït Benhaddou — slow-cooked lamb tagine, couscous with seven vegetables, and fresh-baked bread from a clay oven.
meals.dinner: Intimate dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — Moroccan-Mediterranean fusion menu with wine pairing from a curated cellar.

day_by_day.notes: The Tizi n'Tichka pass road is winding — those prone to motion sickness should take precautions. Mountain temperatures can be cooler — bring a light layer. Photography at Aït Benhaddou is exceptional in late afternoon golden light.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – March 19, 2027 (Journey to the Sahara – Merzouga)
day_by_day.morning: Early private transfer departs for the Sahara Desert — a scenic 8-9 hour drive through dramatic landscapes: palm-filled Draa Valley, rose-red Dadès Gorge, and the Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs. Stop at Skoura Oasis for a short walk through a palm grove and visit to Kasbah Amridil.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Tinghir and the breathtaking Todra Gorge — towering 300-meter limestone canyon walls. Short guided walk through the gorge floor. Arrive at the edge of the Sahara near Merzouga as the golden hour begins.
day_by_day.evening: Mount your private camel and trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes — Morocco's tallest sand dunes reaching 150 meters. Watch the sunset paint the dunes in shades of amber and crimson. Arrive at your exclusive luxury desert camp: private ensuite Berber tent with king bed, solar lighting, and private terrace. Enjoy a traditional desert feast under a sky blazing with stars, with live Gnawa drumming and storytelling by the fire.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — full spread with fresh juices and Moroccan pastries.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort en route — served at a scenic stop in the Dadès Valley with views of rose-red kasbahs.
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the luxury desert camp — Moroccan mezze, slow-roasted lamb mechoui, couscous royale, and traditional pastries under the stars.

day_by_day.notes: The drive is long but extraordinarily scenic — your private driver will manage all stops. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a light scarf for the dunes. Temperatures drop significantly in the desert at night — warm layers are essential. The luxury camp has private ensuite facilities, charging points, and Wi-Fi.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a private guided sunrise camel trek to the highest dune crest — witness one of the most spectacular sunrises on Earth as the Sahara glows gold and pink. Return to camp for a champagne breakfast on your private tent terrace. Optional: private sandboarding session on the dunes with equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: 4x4 desert excursion into the deep Sahara — visit a nomadic Berber family camp for authentic tea ceremony and cultural exchange. Explore fossil sites and ancient geological formations unique to this region. Return to camp for a midday rest and pool relaxation (luxury camps feature plunge pools). Optional: guided meditation session on the dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset photography session on the dunes with a professional photographer (arranged by your butler). Return to camp for a final desert dinner — private table set among the dunes with lanterns, Moroccan rugs, and a bespoke menu. Stargazing session with a telescope guided by your camp's astronomy expert.

meals.breakfast: Champagne sunrise breakfast on the dune crest — freshly baked Moroccan bread, local honey, goat cheese, dates, and Berber coffee.
meals.lunch: Leisurely poolside lunch at the luxury camp — grilled meats, Moroccan salads, fresh fruit platters, and chilled beverages.
meals.dinner: Bespoke private dune dinner — four-course tasting menu featuring Saharan-spiced lamb chops, truffle couscous, and a chocolate-rose dessert with argan oil drizzle.

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise alarm will be around 5:30 AM — absolutely worth it. Professional photography session adds a premium memory to the trip. Sandboarding equipment is provided but wear closed shoes. Stay hydrated throughout the day — desert air is very dry.

day_by_day.morning: Final relaxed morning at the desert camp — enjoy a slow breakfast and last walk among the dunes. Private luxury transfer departs for Marrakech via an alternative scenic route through the Ziz Valley and Erfoud fossil capital. Stop at a premium argan oil cooperative for a guided tour and shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech mid-afternoon. Freshen up at the resort and enjoy a final leisurely afternoon — optional last-minute souk shopping with your private guide for premium Moroccan crafts: hand-knotted Berber rugs, silver jewelry, leather goods, and spice collections. Farewell spa treatment at the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at one of Marrakech's most exclusive venues — La Sultana or Le Tobsil — a romantic candlelit riad experience with a full Moroccan royal feast, live Andalusian orchestra, and a personalized farewell toast arranged by your butler. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final desert camp breakfast — Berber pancakes, fresh dates, honey, and mint tea as the dunes glow in morning light.
meals.lunch: Lunch en route at a premium stop in the Ziz Valley — traditional Moroccan tagine and fresh-squeezed juice at a scenic oasis restaurant.
meals.dinner: Royal farewell dinner at Le Tobsil — a legendary Marrakech riad restaurant with an exquisite 6-course Moroccan feast, live music, and an intimate candlelit courtyard atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time with your butler and arrange airport transfer accordingly. Allow at least 3 hours before flight for Marrakech airport security. Your butler will assist with luggage, packing of any fragile souk purchases, and final checkout formalities. A curated gift hamper of Moroccan argan products, spices, and pastries will be prepared as a farewell gesture from the resort.
